quotes.text: The thing most people miss is that agent autonomy is not a switch, it's an accumulation. Every exception you approve, every temporary permission you never revoke, every environment you mark as temporary test and leave running. These become the scaffolding of irreversible behavior.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains how agent autonomy grows silently through unrevoked exceptions.

quotes.text: A loop is not malicious, it is a function without a termination clause. You forgot to define one. Here's the shortcut nobody teaches. Governance is not a policy PDF. It's executable control.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes governance as enforceable control instead of documentation.

quotes.text: Now you might be thinking the fix is to slow down agents, that is latency disguised as safety. The better method is to constrain capability surfaces and increase observability.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear recommendation: constrain and observe rather than throttle agents.

quotes.text: The reason this works is simple. Agents are amplifiers. They amplify clarity or chaos. When your permissions are precise, they operate precisely. When your policies are ambiguous, they explore ambiguity at machine speed.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable mental model of agents as amplifiers of policy quality.

quotes.text: Co-Pilot did not breach anything, it operated within the permissions you assigned, you called it a leak, it was configuration exposing truth.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shifts blame for Copilot data exposure to permission configuration.

chapters.title: The AI's warning: agents outpacing governance
Root cause: human inconsistency and missing guardrails
Three failure scenarios: loops, Copilot leakage, shadow automation
Minimum viable governance in five phases
Ongoing cadence, kill switches and enforcement cuts
Mapping the EU AI Act to the Microsoft stack

takeaways: Runaway agents, looping Power Automate flows and Copilot oversharing are governance failures caused by inconsistent permissions and policies, not AI rebellion.
A 48-hour baseline of Purview DLP connector blocks, secure agent environments, PIM and Conditional Access, red-team runbooks and audit visibility turns chaos into executable control.
Pre-staged kill switches, weekly drift and shadow automation reviews, and controls mapped to EU AI Act articles keep agents aligned and auditable over time.
hook: Your AI agents, Power Automate flows and Copilot deployments may already be outpacing your governance. This episode is for Microsoft 365 and Power Platform admins and security leads who need a concrete 48-hour plan with DLP, PIM, Conditional Access, Defender for Cloud Apps and kill switches to regain control before shadow automation turns into data loss.
